stimuli.title: Two rows facing south, one behind the other
stimuli.content:
Eight persons Aalok, Binita, Chakshu, Dhanvi, Ehsaan, Fenil, Gauransh and Hetal sit in two rows of four seats each. Everyone faces south. Row 1 is the front row; Row 2 is directly behind it, so each person in Row 2 sits directly behind one person in Row 1. (Facing south, the right is towards the west and the left towards the east.)

- Aalok sits in the front row, second from the right end of that row.
- Gauransh sits directly behind Aalok, and Chakshu sits immediately to the left of Gauransh.
- Dhanvi sits second to the left of Aalok, and Ehsaan sits directly behind Dhanvi.
- Hetal sits in the front row at one of its ends.
- Binita does not sit in the front row.
stimuli.solution:
Number the columns 1 to 4 from the west. Facing south, the right end of a row is its west end.
Step 1: Aalok = Row 1, column 2. Gauransh = Row 2, column 2; Chakshu, to his left (east): Row 2, column 3.
Step 2: Dhanvi is second to Aalok's left: Row 1, column 4; Ehsaan behind her: Row 2, column 4.
Step 3: Free seats: Row 1 columns 1 and 3, Row 2 column 1. Hetal is at an end of the front row: column 1. Binita is not in the front row: Row 2, column 1. Fenil = Row 1, column 3.

| Column (from west) | Row 1 (front) | Row 2 (behind) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hetal | Binita |
| 2 | Aalok | Gauransh |
| 3 | Fenil | Chakshu |
| 4 | Dhanvi | Ehsaan |

stimuli.title: Seven players in a row, with jersey numbers
stimuli.content:
Seven players Kuldeep, Lipsa, Murari, Nandan, Paridhi, Ruchika and Somnath sit in a straight row, all facing north. Their jersey numbers are 7, 9, 10, 14, 18, 21 and 23, a different number for each player. (Facing north, the right is towards the east.)

- Lipsa sits exactly in the middle of the row and wears the smallest number.
- The person wearing 23 sits at the extreme left end of the row.
- Kuldeep sits immediately to the right of Lipsa, and his number is twice Murari's.
- Nandan sits at the extreme right end, and his number is three times Lipsa's.
- Ruchika sits immediately to the left of Nandan, and Somnath sits second to the left of Kuldeep.
- Murari does not sit at an end of the row.
- Somnath's number is greater than Ruchika's.
stimuli.solution:
Number the seats 1 to 7 from the left.
Step 1: Lipsa = 4 (number 7). Kuldeep = 5, Nandan = 7 with 3 × 7 = 21, Ruchika = 6, Somnath = 3.
Step 2: Seats 1 and 2 remain for Murari and Paridhi; Murari is not at an end: Murari = 2, Paridhi = 1. The number 23 is at the left end: Paridhi.
Step 3: 9, 10, 14 and 18 remain for Murari, Somnath, Kuldeep and Ruchika. Kuldeep = 2 × Murari: 18 and 9. Somnath's number is greater than Ruchika's: Somnath 14, Ruchika 10.

| Seat | Player | Number |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Paridhi | 23 |
| 2 | Murari | 9 |
| 3 | Somnath | 14 |
| 4 | Lipsa | 7 |
| 5 | Kuldeep | 18 |
| 6 | Ruchika | 10 |
| 7 | Nandan | 21 |

stimuli.title: Six persons around a round table, with coloured caps
stimuli.content:
Six persons Daya, Kirpal, Nutan, Pinki, Ramesh and Sonu sit around a circular table, equally spaced and all facing the centre. Each wears a cap of a different colour among Black, Green, Orange, Red, White and Yellow. (Facing the centre, a person's right is anticlockwise and the left clockwise.)

- Kirpal sits opposite Daya, and Sonu sits immediately to the left of Kirpal.
- Nutan sits immediately between Daya and Sonu.
- Pinki sits immediately to the left of Daya.
- Daya wears the Red cap, and the person wearing the Green cap sits opposite her.
- The person wearing the White cap sits immediately to the right of Daya.
- The person wearing the Black cap sits second to the left of Ramesh.
- Pinki does not wear the Yellow cap.
stimuli.solution:
Number the seats 0 to 5 anticlockwise from Daya.
Step 1: Kirpal = 3 (opposite). Sonu, to Kirpal's left (clockwise): 2. Nutan sits between Daya and Sonu: 1. Pinki, to Daya's left: 5. Ramesh = 4.
Step 2: Daya Red, Kirpal (opposite) Green, Nutan (Daya's right) White. Black is second to Ramesh's left (clockwise from 4): seat 2, Sonu.
Step 3: Orange and Yellow remain for Ramesh and Pinki; Pinki does not wear Yellow: Pinki Orange, Ramesh Yellow.

| Seat (anticlockwise) | Person | Cap |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Daya | Red |
| 1 | Nutan | White |
| 2 | Sonu | Black |
| 3 | Kirpal | Green |
| 4 | Ramesh | Yellow |
| 5 | Pinki | Orange |

stimuli.title: Eight persons around a round table, with ages
stimuli.content:
Eight persons Akhilesh, Bhagwati, Deepti, Gurmeet, Jasoda, Kamlesh, Neetu and Sahil sit around a circular table, equally spaced and all facing the centre. Their ages are 21, 24, 27, 30, 33, 36, 39 and 42 years, one age each. (Facing the centre, the right is anticlockwise.)

- Sahil sits opposite Akhilesh and is the oldest of all.
- Neetu is the youngest of all and sits immediately to the right of Akhilesh.
- Gurmeet sits second to the left of Sahil and is 18 years older than Neetu.
- Deepti sits immediately to the right of Sahil and is 3 years older than Neetu.
- Kamlesh sits opposite Gurmeet, and Jasoda sits immediately between Gurmeet and Sahil.
- Akhilesh is older than Bhagwati but younger than Kamlesh.
- Jasoda is 3 years younger than Bhagwati.
stimuli.solution:
Number the seats 0 to 7 anticlockwise from Akhilesh.
Step 1: Sahil = 4 (42). Neetu = 1 (21). Gurmeet, second to Sahil's left (clockwise): 2, aged 21 + 18 = 39. Deepti, to Sahil's right: 5, aged 24.
Step 2: Kamlesh is opposite Gurmeet: 6. Jasoda sits between Gurmeet (2) and Sahil (4): 3. Bhagwati = 7.
Step 3: 27, 30, 33 and 36 remain for Akhilesh, Bhagwati, Jasoda and Kamlesh. Jasoda = Bhagwati − 3 and Bhagwati < Akhilesh < Kamlesh: Jasoda 27, Bhagwati 30, Akhilesh 33, Kamlesh 36 (Jasoda 30, Bhagwati 33 would leave Akhilesh younger than Bhagwati).

| 1 | Neetu | 21 |
| 2 | Gurmeet | 39 |
| 3 | Jasoda | 27 |

stimuli.title: Eight persons seated in order of rank
stimuli.content:
Eight persons Aanya, Balwant, Darshana, Gitesh, Himmat, Kesar, Prachi and Shivam sit around a circular table, equally spaced and all facing the centre. They were ranked 1 to 8 in a test (rank 1 is the highest), and they are seated so that the person with each next rank (2 after 1, 3 after 2, and so on up to 8) sits third to the right of the person with the previous rank. (Facing the centre, the right is anticlockwise.)

- Prachi sits second to the left of Himmat, and Shivam sits immediately to the right of Prachi.
- Gitesh sits opposite Kesar, and Aanya sits immediately to the left of Kesar.
- Balwant is ranked last, and Kesar is ranked below Darshana.
stimuli.solution:
Number the seats 0 to 7 anticlockwise from the rank-1 person. Moving three seats right each time, the ranks 1 to 8 sit at seats 0, 3, 6, 1, 4, 7, 2, 5. So seat 0 = rank 1, 1 = rank 4, 2 = rank 7, 3 = rank 2, 4 = rank 5, 5 = rank 8, 6 = rank 3, 7 = rank 6.
Step 1: Balwant (rank 8) = seat 5. Prachi, Shivam and Himmat sit in three consecutive seats p, p + 1, p + 2; Kesar, Aanya and Gitesh satisfy Aanya = Kesar − 1 and Gitesh = Kesar + 4.
Step 2: Avoiding seat 5, the only fits are (a) Prachi 0, Shivam 1, Himmat 2, Gitesh 3, Aanya 6, Kesar 7, Darshana 4, or (b) Prachi 1, Shivam 2, Himmat 3, Kesar 0, Aanya 7, Gitesh 4, Darshana 6.
Step 3: In (b) Kesar would be ranked 1, above Darshana (rank 3) ✗. So (a): Prachi 1, Gitesh 2, Aanya 3, Shivam 4, Darshana 5, Kesar 6, Himmat 7, Balwant 8.

| Seat | Person | Rank |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Prachi | 1 |
| 1 | Shivam | 4 |
| 2 | Himmat | 7 |
| 3 | Gitesh | 2 |
| 4 | Darshana | 5 |
| 5 | Balwant | 8 |
| 6 | Aanya | 3 |
| 7 | Kesar | 6 |

stimuli.title: Seven floors and seven fruits
stimuli.content:
Seven persons Bunty, Chikki, Golu, Jugnu, Minku, Pappu and Tinku live on the seven floors of a building, one on each floor (floor 1 is the lowermost, floor 7 the topmost). Each likes a different fruit among Apple, Banana, Grapes, Guava, Mango, Orange and Papaya.

- Minku lives on floor 4 and likes Orange.
- Chikki lives immediately above Minku, and Bunty lives immediately below Minku.
- Pappu lives on the topmost floor, and Jugnu lives between Chikki and Pappu.
- Golu lives below Tinku.
- The person who likes Mango lives immediately below the person who likes Orange, and the person who likes Grapes lives two floors above the Mango lover.
- The person on the topmost floor likes Papaya, and Golu likes Guava.
- Tinku does not like Banana.
stimuli.solution:
Step 1: Minku = 4 (Orange), Chikki = 5, Bunty = 3, Pappu = 7, Jugnu = 6 (between 5 and 7).
Step 2: Floors 1 and 2 remain for Golu and Tinku; Golu is below: Golu = 1, Tinku = 2.
Step 3: Mango is immediately below Orange: floor 3 (Bunty). Grapes is two floors above Mango: floor 5 (Chikki). Papaya: floor 7 (Pappu). Golu: Guava.
Step 4: Apple and Banana remain for Tinku (2) and Jugnu (6); Tinku does not like Banana: Tinku Apple, Jugnu Banana.

| Floor | Person | Fruit |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | Pappu | Papaya |
| 6 | Jugnu | Banana |
| 5 | Chikki | Grapes |
| 4 | Minku | Orange |
| 3 | Bunty | Mango |
| 2 | Tinku | Apple |
| 1 | Golu | Guava |

stimuli.title: Ten residents in a five-storey building with two flats per floor
stimuli.content:
Ten persons Ajit, Bimla, Chaman, Dharmesh, Ekam, Firoza, Gaurangi, Hardik, Ishita and Jaggi live in a five-storey building (floor 1 is the lowermost). Each floor has two flats, West and East; each West flat is directly above the West flat of the floor below, and likewise for the East flats. One person lives in each flat.

- Ajit lives in the West flat of floor 3, and Gaurangi lives in the other flat on his floor.
- Jaggi lives directly above Gaurangi, and Bimla lives directly above Jaggi.
- Hardik lives on the topmost floor, and Ekam lives directly below Hardik.
- Chaman lives in an East flat on a floor below Ajit's.
- Ishita lives on the lowermost floor, and Firoza lives directly above Dharmesh.
stimuli.solution:
Step 1: Ajit = 3 West, Gaurangi = 3 East, Jaggi = 4 East, Bimla = 5 East.
Step 2: Hardik is on floor 5; the East flat is Bimla's, so Hardik = 5 West and Ekam = 4 West.
Step 3: Chaman is in an East flat below floor 3: 1 East or 2 East. Firoza is directly above Dharmesh: the free stacked pairs are 1–2 West and 1–2 East, and the East pair would leave no East flat for Chaman, so Dharmesh = 1 West, Firoza = 2 West.
Step 4: Ishita is on floor 1: 1 East. Chaman = 2 East.

| Floor | West | East |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | Hardik | Bimla |
| 4 | Ekam | Jaggi |
| 3 | Ajit | Gaurangi |
| 2 | Firoza | Chaman |
| 1 | Dharmesh | Ishita |

stimuli.title: Six floors, six pets and six drinks
stimuli.content:
Six persons Lakhan, Mili, Nirja, Omi, Rasika and Taran live on the six floors of a building, one on each floor (floor 1 is the lowermost). Each owns a different pet among a Cat, a Dog, a Fish, a Hamster, a Parrot and a Rabbit, and each drinks a different one of Coffee, Juice, Lassi, Milk, Soup and Tea.

- Lakhan lives on an even-numbered floor and owns the Cat.
- The Fish owner lives immediately below the Cat owner.
- Nirja lives on the topmost floor and drinks Lassi.
- Omi lives somewhere between Lakhan and Nirja.
- The Rabbit owner drinks Juice and lives immediately below the Lassi drinker.
- Taran lives on the lowermost floor and drinks Tea; Mili lives immediately above Taran and owns the Dog.
- Rasika drinks Coffee.
- The Hamster owner lives above the Parrot owner, and the Milk drinker lives above the Soup drinker.
stimuli.solution:
Step 1: Nirja = 6 (Lassi). Taran = 1 (Tea), Mili = 2 (Dog).
Step 2: The Rabbit owner, who drinks Juice, is on floor 5. Lakhan (Cat) is on an even floor: 4 (2 is Mili's), so the Fish is on floor 3.
Step 3: Omi lives between Lakhan (4) and Nirja (6): 5, so Omi owns the Rabbit and drinks Juice. Rasika = 3 (Fish) and drinks Coffee.
Step 4: Hamster and Parrot remain for Nirja (6) and Taran (1); the Hamster is higher: Nirja Hamster, Taran Parrot. Milk and Soup remain for Lakhan (4) and Mili (2); Milk is higher: Lakhan Milk, Mili Soup.

| Floor | Person | Pet | Drink |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | Nirja | Hamster | Lassi |
| 5 | Omi | Rabbit | Juice |
| 4 | Lakhan | Cat | Milk |
| 3 | Rasika | Fish | Coffee |
| 2 | Mili | Dog | Soup |
| 1 | Taran | Parrot | Tea |

stimuli.title: Five Greek capital letters for comparisons
stimuli.content:
In the questions of this set, the Greek capital letters Γ, Λ, Ξ, Π and Ψ are used with these meanings:
'A Γ B' means 'A is greater than B'; 'A Λ B' means 'A is smaller than B'; 'A Ξ B' means 'A is either greater than or equal to B'; 'A Π B' means 'A is either smaller than or equal to B'; 'A Ψ B' means 'A is equal to B'.
Assuming the statements to be true, find which of the conclusions I and II is/are definitely true.
stimuli.solution: Decode: Γ means >, Λ means <, Ξ means ≥, Π means ≤ and Ψ means =. Rewrite the statements with ordinary signs, join them into a chain and test each conclusion.

stimuli.title: Five chess symbols defined by negations
stimuli.content:
In the questions of this set, chess symbols are used between two letters with these meanings:
'A ♔ B' means 'A is neither smaller than nor equal to B'; 'A ♕ B' means 'A is not greater than B'; 'A ♖ B' means 'A is neither greater than nor smaller than B'; 'A ♗ B' means 'A is not smaller than B'; 'A ♘ B' means 'A is neither greater than nor equal to B'.
Assuming the statements to be true, find which of the conclusions I and II is/are definitely true.
stimuli.solution: Translate each negation: 'neither smaller nor equal' = >, 'not greater' = ≤, 'neither greater nor smaller' = =, 'not smaller' = ≥, 'neither greater nor equal' = <. So ♔ is >, ♕ is ≤, ♖ is =, ♗ is ≥ and ♘ is <. Then join the statements into one chain.

stimuli.title: Six treks in six months, read by season
stimuli.content:
Six friends Aadi, Bela, Daksh, Hema, Ishan and Kajal each go on one trek in the same year, in six different months among January, March, April, July, October and December. Take the seasons as: Spring = January to March, Summer = April to June, Monsoon = July to September, Winter = October to December.

- Hema treks in the only Summer month among the six.
- Ishan treks in a Monsoon month.
- Kajal treks in the month that comes just before Hema's among the six months.
- Daksh and Bela both trek in Winter, and Bela's month is later.
stimuli.solution:
Of the six months, only April is in Summer: Hema. Only July is in Monsoon: Ishan. The month before April in the list is March: Kajal. Winter months are October and December; Bela is later, so Daksh October and Bela December. Aadi takes the remaining month, January.

Jan Aadi, Mar Kajal, Apr Hema, Jul Ishan, Oct Daksh, Dec Bela.

stimuli.title: Six appointments across the end of September 2026
stimuli.content:
Six persons Pranav, Rukmini, Sachin, Tanvi, Uttam and Vidya each have one appointment at a passport office on six different dates from Friday, 25 September 2026 to Tuesday, 6 October 2026 (September has 30 days).

- Rukmini's appointment is on the last day of September.
- Pranav's appointment is exactly five days after Rukmini's.
- Tanvi's appointment is on the first Saturday of the period.
- Vidya's appointment is on a Friday in October.
- Sachin's appointment is on the day after Vidya's.
- Uttam's appointment is on a Monday, before Rukmini's.
stimuli.solution:
Days: Fri 25, Sat 26, Sun 27, Mon 28, Tue 29, Wed 30 September; Thu 1, Fri 2, Sat 3, Sun 4, Mon 5, Tue 6 October. Rukmini 30 September; Pranav five days later, 5 October. Tanvi: first Saturday, 26 September. Vidya: the Friday in October, 2 October; Sachin 3 October. Uttam: a Monday before 30 September, 28 September.

Tanvi 26 Sep (Sat), Uttam 28 Sep (Mon), Rukmini 30 Sep (Wed), Vidya 2 Oct (Fri), Sachin 3 Oct (Sat), Pranav 5 Oct (Mon).

stimuli.title: Six employees and their retirement years
stimuli.content:
Six employees Gyan, Hridya, Kesar, Lohit, Mrinal and Navya of a bank were born in six different years between 1960 and 1995. Each employee retires in the year in which he or she turns 60.

- Kesar retires in 2031.
- Lohit is seven years younger than Kesar.
- Gyan retires in 2026, and Navya is exactly ten years younger than Gyan.
- Hridya was born in a leap year, after Kesar but before Lohit.
- Mrinal is the youngest of the six, and Mrinal's age in 2026 is a perfect square.
stimuli.solution:
Kesar: 2031 − 60 = 1971; Lohit 1978. Gyan: 2026 − 60 = 1966; Navya 1976. Hridya: a leap year after 1971 and before 1978 — 1972 or 1976 — and 1976 is Navya's, so 1972. Mrinal is the youngest (after 1978) and is a perfect-square age in 2026: 36 (born 1990) is the only one within 1979–1995 (25 would be 2001, 49 would be 1977).

Birth / retirement: Gyan 1966/2026, Kesar 1971/2031, Hridya 1972/2032, Navya 1976/2036, Lohit 1978/2038, Mrinal 1990/2050.

stimuli.title: Three departments, two posts each, six joining years
stimuli.content:
Six employees Aarav, Bhakti, Chaitali, Devesh, Eeshan and Fiza work in three departments of a company — HR, IT and Sales. Each holds one of two posts, Manager or Executive, and each joined in a different year from 2018 to 2023.

- Each department has exactly two of them: one Manager and one Executive, and in each department the Manager joined earlier than the Executive.
- Aarav, an Executive, joined last of the six.
- Devesh joined first of the six, and Bhakti works in the same department as Devesh.
- Fiza is a Manager and joined one year after Devesh.
- Chaitali works in Sales and joined in 2020.
- Eeshan joined in the year after Chaitali and works in the same department as her.
- Bhakti does not work in IT.
stimuli.solution:
Aarav joined in 2023 as an Executive; Devesh in 2018. Devesh joined before everyone, so he cannot be an Executive (his Manager would have joined earlier): Devesh is a Manager, and Bhakti, in his department, is its Executive. Fiza: Manager, 2019. Chaitali: Sales, 2020; Eeshan: Sales, 2021 — so Chaitali is the Sales Manager and Eeshan the Sales Executive. Sales is full, so Devesh and Bhakti are in HR or IT; Bhakti is not in IT, so both are in HR. Fiza then manages IT and Aarav is the IT Executive. Bhakti takes the remaining year, 2022.

HR: Devesh (Manager, 2018), Bhakti (Executive, 2022); IT: Fiza (Manager, 2019), Aarav (Executive, 2023); Sales: Chaitali (Manager, 2020), Eeshan (Executive, 2021).

stimuli.title: A family of six across three generations
stimuli.content:
A family has six members — Gunjan, Harsh, Indira, Jatin, Kirti and Lavanya — across three generations, with exactly two married couples.

- Harsh is married to Indira.
- Gunjan is the only grandchild of Indira and is a girl.
- Lavanya is the daughter-in-law of Harsh.
- Jatin is the father of Gunjan.
- Kirti is unmarried and is the sister-in-law of Lavanya.
stimuli.solution:
Lavanya, Harsh's daughter-in-law, is married to a son of Harsh; Jatin is Gunjan's father and Gunjan is Indira's grandchild, so Jatin is that son and Lavanya his wife. Kirti is unmarried, so as Lavanya's sister-in-law she must be her husband's sister: Harsh's daughter.
Tree: Harsh + Indira → Jatin (+ Lavanya) → Gunjan; Kirti.

stimuli.title: A family of eight with two cousins
stimuli.content:
A family has eight members — Bhola, Charu, Divya, Eshan, Faiz, Gita, Hiten and Ira — across three generations, with three married couples. Every spouse is a member of the family.

- Bhola is Charu's husband, and Eshan is their only son.
- Divya is a daughter of Bhola.
- Faiz is the son-in-law of Bhola.
- Gita is the mother of Ira and the sister-in-law of Divya.
- Hiten (a boy) and Ira (a girl) are the only grandchildren of Charu, and they are cousins.
stimuli.solution:
Faiz, Bhola's son-in-law, is married to Bhola's daughter Divya (the only daughter in the family). Gita is Divya's sister-in-law and not Faiz's wife, so she is Eshan's wife; Ira's mother is Gita, so Ira is Eshan's daughter. Hiten, the other grandchild and Ira's cousin, is the son of Divya and Faiz.
Tree: Bhola + Charu → Divya (+ Faiz) → Hiten; Eshan (+ Gita) → Ira.

stimuli.title: Six trees and their heights
stimuli.content:
Six trees P, Q, R, S, T and U in a garden have different heights.

- Tree R is taller than exactly four of the other trees.
- Tree Q is taller than tree T but shorter than tree U.
- Tree P is shorter than tree T.
- Exactly one tree is taller than tree S and shorter than tree R.
stimuli.solution: R is the 2nd tallest. U > Q > T > P, so U is the tallest. S is two places below R, that is, 4th tallest; Q, T and P fill the 3rd, 5th and 6th places in that order. Tallest to shortest: U, R, Q, S, T, P.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Five persons Ganga, Hemu, Indra, Jolly and Kamal sit in a straight row, all facing south. (For a person facing south, the right is towards the west and the left is towards the east.)
- Ganga sits exactly in the middle of the row, and Indra sits immediately to her left.
- Hemu sits at an extreme end of the row, next to Indra.
- Jolly does not sit next to Ganga.

Who sits at the extreme right end of the row?

solution.concept: Facing south, the right end of the row is its west end
solution.explanation: Number the seats 1 to 5 from the west. Ganga = 3; her left is east, so Indra = 4, and Hemu, at an end next to Indra, = 5. Jolly cannot sit next to Ganga, so Jolly = 1 and Kamal = 2. The right end (west end) is seat 1: Jolly.
steps: Jolly not next to Ganga ⇒ Jolly 1, Kamal 2
Right end = west end = seat 1 ⇒ Jolly
solution.why_others_wrong: Hemu is at the left (east) end; Kamal and Indra are not at an end.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability

solution.explanation: Combined: K < D ≤ P = Y > G ≥ N > Z. K and G lie on opposite sides of the turn at Y, so K < G is not certain (I). P = Y > G ≥ N gives P > N (II), and Z < N ≤ G < Y = P gives Z < P (III).
steps: Chain: K < D ≤ P = Y > G ≥ N > Z
I: turn at Y ⇒ not certain
solution.why_others_wrong: 'All three' accepts I, which crosses the turn at Y; 'Only II' misses III; 'None' misses both.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Only II and III are true

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: In which of the following expressions is 'M ≥ C' definitely true, but 'M > C' not definitely true?

solution.concept: '≥' certain but '>' not: the path must avoid every strict sign
solution.explanation: In M ≥ T = R ≥ C ≤ B, the path from M to C has only '≥' and '=' signs, so M ≥ C is certain but M = C is still possible — M > C is not certain.
steps: Need: path M → C with no turn and no strict sign
M ≥ T = R ≥ C: only ≥ and = ⇒ M ≥ C, not M > C
solution.why_others_wrong: M ≥ T > R = C and B ≤ M > T = R ≥ C contain a strict sign, so M > C is definitely true as well; M = T ≥ R ≤ C turns at R, so even M ≥ C is not certain.
solution.final_answer: Option B: M ≥ T = R ≥ C ≤ B

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Who treks in January?

solution.explanation: Every other month is taken by a clue, so Aadi gets January.
steps: Jan Aadi, Mar Kajal, Apr Hema, Jul Ishan, Oct Daksh, Dec Bela
solution.why_others_wrong: Kajal treks in March, Daksh in October and Bela in December.

questions.question_text: How many friends trek between Kajal and Bela?

questions.question_text: In which month does Ishan trek?

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Who treks in the month that comes immediately after Ishan's among the six months?

solution.explanation: After July comes October: Daksh.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: How many of the friends trek in a month that has 31 days?

solution.explanation: January, March, July, October and December have 31 days; only April has 30. So five friends.

31-day months: Jan, Mar, Jul, Oct, Dec ⇒ 5

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
In a certain month, the 14th is a Wednesday. Leena's birthday is on the 14th. Manas's birthday is three days after Leena's, and Nirav's birthday is on the Monday of the same week (the week runs from Monday to Sunday).

On which date is Nirav's birthday, and on which day of the week is Manas's birthday?

solution.concept: Count days forwards and backwards
solution.explanation: The Monday of the week that holds Wednesday the 14th is two days earlier: the 12th. Manas: 14 + 3 = 17th; Wednesday + 3 days = Saturday.
solution.why_others_wrong: 13th is a Tuesday; Friday is the 16th, only two days after Leena's; 11th is the Sunday of the previous week.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text:
Four siblings Jugal, Kirti, Lakshmi and Mohan were born in 2001, 2004, 2007 and 2010, one in each year. Ages are counted in completed years on their birthdays.
- Kirti is the eldest.
- Mohan is younger than Jugal but older than Lakshmi.

How old will Mohan be on his birthday in 2026?

solution.concept: Order of birth years
solution.explanation: Kirti is the eldest: 2001. Jugal is older than Mohan, who is older than Lakshmi: Jugal 2004, Mohan 2007, Lakshmi 2010. In 2026 Mohan turns 2026 − 2007 = 19.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability

Four friends Rina, Sohan, Tara and Uday each start a monthly savings plan in a different month of the same year.

- Tara starts two months before Sohan.
- Uday starts in the month immediately after Tara's.

Who starts in June?

solution.explanation: Rina: March. Sohan: March + 4 = July. Tara: July − 2 = May. Uday: May + 1 = June.
steps: Rina Mar ⇒ Sohan Jul ⇒ Tara May ⇒ Uday Jun
solution.why_others_wrong: Tara starts in May, Sohan in July and Rina in March.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability

questions.question_text: How many days after Tanvi's appointment is Pranav's appointment?

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: On which day of the week is Rukmini's appointment?

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Who retires in 2036?

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: In which year will Mrinal retire?

solution.explanation: Mrinal must be younger than Lohit (1978) and born by 1995: age in 2026 between 31 and 47. The only perfect square there is 36, so Mrinal was born in 1990 and retires in 2050.

questions.question_text: Who retires immediately after Kesar?

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: How many of the six were born in a leap year?

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability

Five colleagues Ujala, Vimal, Waseem, Xenia and Yatin reached the office at different times on Monday.

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: Who is the Manager of the IT department?

questions.subject: Reasoning Ability
questions.question_text: In which year did Bhakti join?

questions.question_text: How many Executives joined before 2023?
